proposal.title: Vactosertib + peptide vaccine + Anktiva + checkpoint blockade
proposal.status_label: Proposed with Dr Kesari / Asthra — not started
proposal.body: I am planning a combination with Dr Santosh Kesari at Asthra Health: vactosertib, my personalised JLF peptide vaccine, N-803 (Anktiva) and checkpoint blockade. Pembrolizumab is the PD-1 option discussed; BOT/BAL is an alternative requiring renewed approval. Manufacturing was reported successful for 19 of 20 vaccine targets, which does not confirm final batch release or administration. Hiltonol/poly-ICLC is the intended adjuvant.
proposal.rationale: The vaccine aims to prime tumour-specific T cells, vactosertib to reduce TGF-beta-mediated suppression, N-803 to support NK/CD8-cell expansion, and checkpoint blockade to sustain immune activity. My archival data suggest weak recruitment and a stromal treated-resection phenotype, but do not establish which barrier dominates current disease.
proposal.evidence_summary: Human studies support immune effects of these components, and vactosertib/pembrolizumab produced 13 responses among 103 evaluable colorectal-cancer patients. That overall denominator was not exclusively confirmed MSS. The exact four-component regimen has not established efficacy or safety, especially after prior BOT/BAL. My completed trial-RNA analysis did not identify a positive TGF-beta/fibroblast response marker.
decision_points: Vactosertib: Dr Kesari has identified a single-patient access route through Asthra. Sponsor agreement, approvals and supply remain to be confirmed.

Peptide vaccine: delivery through Asthra has been discussed. Confirm the released product, selected peptides, adjuvant and schedule with the vaccine team; manufacturing success is not a final release or administration record.

N-803 (Anktiva): access through Asthra has been discussed. Systemic use for CRC is investigational; the team must confirm formulation, route and access arrangements. Licensed intravesical bladder-cancer use does not establish efficacy or safety for this route or regimen.

Checkpoint blockade: pembrolizumab is the discussed PD-1 option. BOT/BAL would replace that checkpoint component, adding CTLA-4 blockade; further supply requires a new clinical rationale and sponsor approval after my previous progression.

Review retained and expressed mutant targets, exact peptide sequences, HLA restrictions and CD4/CD8 coverage. Predicted binding and vaccine-specific blood responses do not prove recognition of the cancer.

Agree sequencing, monitoring and how this fits around current systemic treatment. Dendritic-cell function, recruitment and tumour entry remain potential gaps; the proposal does not assume that additional drugs will solve them.
proposal.timing: I am aiming to begin the vaccine in early 2027. The complete combination, access approvals, final batch release and start date remain to be agreed with my treating team; no component is recorded as started as part of this proposal.
proposal.public_caveat: This is a concrete treatment proposal with access discussions underway, not an administered or clinically validated regimen. Current systemic treatment is documented separately.

proposal.access_summary: Asthra has discussed vaccine delivery and N-803 access. On 6 November, Dr Kesari said his team would add me to the vactosertib single-patient IND access list. Final approvals, supply and the full schedule remain to be agreed.

research_leads.mechanism: Expands dendritic cells that present vaccine antigens to T cells
research_leads.evidence_type: Randomized human melanoma immunogenicity; early combination trials
research_leads.evidence: Randomized melanoma vaccine study improved DC abundance and antigen-specific immunity; CRC benefit is unestablished.
research_leads.display_evidence: Randomized melanoma vaccine study improved DC abundance and antigen-specific immunity; CRC benefit is unestablished.
research_leads.access: Relevant melanoma trial closed to recruitment. Celldex physician enquiry possible; current supply and compassionate access unconfirmed.
research_leads.caveat: A distinct DC-support research lead; this is not an efficacy-rank upgrade or a substitute for DC activation.

priority.rationale: Lower-confidence research option: a plausible priming or immune-metabolism role, without demonstrated CRC benefit from this intervention or its addition to the proposed combination. Access is assessed separately.

details.stage: Clinical-stage DC-expansion strategy. NCT04930783 pairs NeoVax/CDX-301 with PD-1 blockade in melanoma; registry is Active, not recruiting, updated 25 March 2026, actual enrolment 10. NCT05029999 remains Recruiting but is restricted to HER2-negative breast cancer and combines CDX-301/CDX-1140 with liposomal doxorubicin.
details.patient_evidence: Poor recruitment signals support exploring stronger vaccine priming, but archival DC-associated markers are mixed. These bulk data do not establish a global DC shortage or predict FLT3L response. N-803 primarily expands NK/CD8 cells, so FLT3L addresses a different step.
details.clinical_evidence: Randomized phase II melanoma vaccine study demonstrated increased DC abundance and stronger antigen-specific immune responses; clinical efficacy in CRC and contribution to the proposed combination remain unestablished.
details.access: No open CRC-specific route verified. Relevant NeoVax/CDX-301 melanoma study is closed to recruitment. Celldex permits physician enquiries, but its currently linked May 2018 compassionate-use policy says no products are available; current CDX-301 supply and any individual request require direct sponsor confirmation.
details.timing: Explore only as a coordinated vaccine-priming strategy with antigen and innate adjuvant. No validated sequence with vactosertib, N-803 and checkpoint blockade is established; expansion alone does not restore malignant-cell peptide-HLA display.
details.evidence_level: Randomized human melanoma immunogenicity; early combination trials; no validated personal response prediction
details.safety: Human immune-response studies provide early tolerability information, but the safety of adding CDX-301 to this full combination is unknown. Expansion of APCs does not guarantee a productive antitumour response.

details.stage: Broad phase I NCT03329950, which included CRC among eligible cancers, is Completed (132 actual enrolment; updated 28 March 2024). Personalized TCR-T/CDX-1140/pembrolizumab NCT05349890 is Active, not recruiting. USC in-situ CDX-301/radiotherapy/CDX-1140/poly-ICLC NCT04616248 is Active, not recruiting and its specified diagnoses exclude CRC. Other CDX-1140 trials remain active in non-CRC cancers, so the whole programme should not be labelled discontinued.
details.patient_evidence: Low recruitment and mixed DC-associated archival markers make APC function a research question. They do not show CD40 dependence or provide a validated response selector. Better priming would still require useful vaccine targets and tumour-cell antigen display.
details.clinical_evidence: Early local CDX-1140/peptide/poly-ICLC melanoma experience supports feasibility and some immune responses; no randomized CRC benefit or safety of adding systemic CD40 stimulation to the proposed regimen is established.
details.access: No currently open CRC CDX-1140 route verified. Celldex's general physician-enquiry policy does not establish available drug; its linked older policy explicitly says products are unavailable for compassionate use. Agent-specific supply and eligibility need confirmation. M0324, a MUC1-conditional CD40 agonist, has a Recruiting phase I trial NCT07166601 (updated 2 November 2026), with US sites. Public eligibility names selected MUC1-overexpressing solid tumours but does not enumerate CRC; do not describe it as a confirmed CRC route. Its pembrolizumab part requires prior ICI progression. NG-350A rectal-cancer FORTRESS NCT06459869 is Active, not recruiting and principally a neoadjuvant locally advanced rectal-cancer strategy, not a matched route for previously resected metastatic disease.
details.timing: Coordinate with antigen delivery and innate adjuvant if studied. No evidence supports adding CD40 empirically as a fifth systemic agent to the proposed four-component regimen.
details.evidence_level: Early human local vaccine study; completed systemic phase I; no validated personal response prediction
details.safety: The 22-person local melanoma vaccine study reported no dose-limiting or grade 3+ treatment-related toxicity. Local exposure in that small study does not establish safety of systemic CD40 agonism or the full proposed combination.

research_leads.evidence_type: Small single-arm human melanoma vaccine study
research_leads.evidence: NeoVaxMI: 10 vaccinated, nine completed; CD8 responses in 6/9. Small melanoma study cannot establish CRC benefit.

research_leads.access: Published trial closed to recruitment and melanoma-specific. Any adaptation requires an agreed clinician-led vaccine protocol.
research_leads.caveat: Poly-ICLC is already intended for my vaccine. Local ipilimumab evidence does not establish benefit from repeating systemic BOT/BAL.

details.stage: NCT03929029 is Active, not recruiting (updated 5 January 2026; actual enrolment 11), melanoma-specific. This is a formulation/local-priming precedent, not a distinct commercially supplied regimen.
details.patient_evidence: Poor immune recruitment makes vaccine potency and coordinated CD4/CD8 priming relevant. The opportunity is to review the actual formulation and delivery of the available peptide vaccine; historical checkpoint exposure does not establish the response to this different local design.
details.clinical_evidence: NeoVaxMI combined long peptides, poly-ICLC, Montanide, vaccine-site ipilimumab and systemic nivolumab: 11 enrolled, 10 vaccinated, 9 completed; ex-vivo CD8 responses in 6/9 fully vaccinated. Predominantly resected melanoma, single-arm; clinical effects and each component's contribution cannot be isolated.
details.access: The published NeoVaxMI trial is closed to recruitment and melanoma-specific. Any adaptation to the existing peptide vaccine would require a clinician-led protocol, suitable product/formulation and coordinated local administration; no established CRC access programme for the full design was identified.
details.timing: Resolve peptide pools, antigen/adjuvant co-delivery and intended local versus systemic components before changing the regimen. No clinical evidence establishes an optimal schedule for this CRC combination.
details.evidence_level: Small single-arm human melanoma vaccine study; no validated personal response prediction
details.safety: NeoVaxMI reported no grade 3/4 vaccine dose-limiting toxicity, but only 10 patients were vaccinated and most had resected melanoma. Local injection-site effects occurred; limited exposure cannot predict toxicity with systemic CTLA-4, N-803 or vactosertib.

research_leads.display_evidence: BAY-8002 rescued DC function ex vivo. Separate AZD3965 phase I experience showed no objective solid-tumour responses.

details.stage: AZD3965 NCT01791595 is Completed (53 enrolled across escalation and lymphoma expansion; updated 11 April 2022). The sponsor's HRA-hosted results summary says no further trials were planned at the time of that summary. Current registry search found only that AZD3965 study. BAY-8002 remains a research reagent in the cited immune experiments; no clinical access route verified.
details.patient_evidence: Existing bulk RNA/protein data do not directly measure DC lactate flux or demonstrate lactate-driven immune dysfunction. Transporter abundance alone would not establish the relevant cellular mechanism or predict benefit.
details.clinical_evidence: The cited DC-rescue paper used BAY-8002 in human ex-vivo melanoma/DC experiments; this was not an AZD3965 therapeutic trial. AZD3965 provides separate early human MCT1-inhibitor experience: 42 enrolled/40 treated in solid-tumour escalation, including 20 enrolled with CRC; no objective responses, nine of 39 baseline-assessed patients had stable disease. Retinal, cardiac-troponin and acidosis toxicities limited dose.
details.access: No active CRC MCT1-inhibitor trial or established expanded-access supply identified. AZD3965's completed trial is clinical precedent, not an available treatment route; BAY-8002's laboratory availability is not clinical availability.
details.timing: A downstream research lead rather than an immediate vaccine add-on. No validated combination schedule or evidence that systemic inhibition improves vaccine responses in CRC exists.
details.evidence_level: Human ex-vivo mechanism; separate phase I MCT1-inhibitor precedent; no validated personal response prediction
details.safety: AZD3965 produced dose-limiting retinal-test changes, cardiac troponin elevation and acidosis. Those human findings matter despite the separate ex-vivo immune rationale; they do not establish the safety of BAY-8002 or a vaccine combination.

research_leads.evidence: Mouse melanoma study supports combination research. Historical BSO/melphalan human use does not demonstrate CRC vaccine benefit.
research_leads.display_evidence: Mouse melanoma study supports combination research. Historical BSO/melphalan human use does not demonstrate CRC vaccine benefit.
research_leads.access: No active matched therapeutic trial or established clinical supply identified; historic BSO studies are completed or withdrawn.

details.stage: Therapeutic registry records identified were completed neuroblastoma trials NCT00005835/NCT00002730 and a withdrawn melanoma limb-infusion trial NCT00661336. No active BSO/DC-vaccine or CRC therapeutic study identified. An unrelated ovarian specimen-screening record appears in a broad search and is not BSO treatment access.
details.patient_evidence: Available case data do not establish glutathione dependence or show that GCL inhibition would selectively improve APC function. This remains a low-confidence research hypothesis.
details.clinical_evidence: The 2026 immune rationale comes from a spontaneous melanoma mouse model: BSO/glutathione depletion combined with DC-expanding/activating immunotherapy delayed tumour growth. BSO has historical human phase I experience with melphalan, including stem-cell-supported neuroblastoma treatment; it is therefore inaccurate to say BSO has never been administered to humans. Those studies do not demonstrate safe or effective CRC vaccine augmentation.
details.access: Research lead with no active matched trial or established clinical supply identified. Historical investigational manufacture and chemotherapy combinations do not establish current access or safety with this vaccine regimen.
details.timing: No validated vaccine, N-803, checkpoint or vactosertib combination schedule. Historical chemotherapy dosing and formulation cannot be transferred to an immune-priming strategy.
details.evidence_level: Preclinical melanoma immune combination; historical human chemotherapy combinations; no validated personal response prediction
details.safety: Glutathione supports normal-cell as well as tumour-cell function. Historical BSO/melphalan studies involved substantial chemotherapy toxicity and, in neuroblastoma, stem-cell support; they cannot establish safety of immune augmentation or be attributed wholly to BSO.
